[MUQATIL:56:1-2/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The Event is the first blast, a cry.
[SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكنهأتملسكونماقبلهومابعده#779/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some lexical patterns are kept intact because they do not follow a verb pattern; surrounding consonant quiescence also favors retention, as with gemination before a quiescent consonant.
[SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكنهأتملسكونماقبلهومابعده#779/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The weak radicals in ʿajūz, risāla, and ṣaḥīfa are hamzated in their plurals because they are originally quiescent, unlike roots that take vowels; after alif they are especially liable to hamza.
[SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكنهأتملسكونماقبلهومابعده#779/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The fāʿil forms from ʿawirat and ṣīdat are ʿāwir and ṣāyid, preserving their weak radicals as in šawayt and ḥayiyt, though assimilation does not apply.
[SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكنهأتملسكونماقبلهومابعده#779/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Fawāʿil plurals from ʿawirat and ṣīdat take hamza by analogy with šawāyā and other hamzated plurals; the heavy meeting of two wāws also supports the change.
[SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكنهأتملسكونماقبلهومابعده#779/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When a noun is formed first and then pluralized, as in taqāwul and tabāyuʿ, hamza is not introduced: the weak radical was originally vowelled, as in maʿūna and maʿīša.
[SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكنهأتملسكونماقبلهومابعده#779/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Many derived noun patterns retain wāw or yāʾ rather than hamzating them; Sībawayh lists forms such as ʿawār, qawwāl, and miqwāl.
[SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكنهأتملسكونماقبلهومابعده#779/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعض العرب | reports | Some Arabs say abyanāʾ, with a quiescent yāʾ and a vowel on bāʾ to avoid kasra on yāʾ; Sībawayh says this is not regular.
[SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكنهأتملسكونماقبلهومابعده#779/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The verbal nouns iqāma and istiqāma are defective because they remain closely tied to their derived verbs; as independent triliteral verbal nouns, they would retain the full form.
[SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكنهأتملسكونماقبلهومابعده#779/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The passive participle mafʿūl is shortened and made quiescent because it is the noun of its verb, so it follows the verb in defectiveness; other cited forms are not verb-nouns.
[SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكنهأتملسكونماقبلهومابعده#779/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Ṭawīl is not formed on yaṭūlu; if it were the verb-based noun, it would be ṭāʾil. It instead patterns as faʿīl with a passive sense and preserves the root, as in makhyūṭ.
[SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكنهأتملسكونماقبلهومابعده#779/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Maqāwil and maʿāyish are not hamzated because they are plurals of maqāla and maʿīša, whose original vowels remain; they are not nouns patterned on the verb.
[SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكنهأتملسكونماقبلهومابعده#779/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Khalīl explains that mafʿal is retained because it is essentially shortened from mifʿāl; the patterns share adjectival meaning and can alternate, as in maftaḥ and miftāḥ.
[SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكنهأتملسكونماقبلهومابعده#779/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | rejects | Sībawayh calls maṣāʾib an error from treating maṣība as faʿīla; it is mafʿila, and maṣāwib is also attested.

[ZAJJAJ:v5p107/r2] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Al-Wāqiʿa here is the Hour and Resurrection.

[NAHHAS:v4p321/r1] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | Idhā is an accusative time adverb governed by waqaʿat; because it resembles a conditional particle it normally takes what follows as its governor.
[NAHHAS:v4p321/r2] NAHHAS, d. 338 · سيبويه | reports | Sibawayh reports that some Arabs put idhā in the jussive, an analogy to conditionals that is strong but used only in poetry.
[NAHHAS:v4p321/r3] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | Unlike a conditional, idhā introduces a specified time, as in I will come when the dates redden; the conditional reading cannot use an or similar open-ended timing.
[NAHHAS:v4p321/r4] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | The feminine tāʾ in waqaʿat takes kasra to avoid two adjacent sukuns because the particle's default is sukun.
[NAHHAS:v4p321/r5] NAHHAS, d. 338 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas says names such as al-Wāqiʿa, al-Tāmma, and al-Ṣākhkha magnify the Resurrection and warn God's servants.
[NAHHAS:v4p321/r6] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | reports | Another view identifies al-Wāqiʿa as the first blast.

[SULAMI:v2p299/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · ابن عطاء | reports | The Event is when the seeker’s intended purpose becomes clear.

[QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r1] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | God's name is overpowering: He brings the attentive near through grace, may remove choice from one persisting in disobedience, and can compel obedience through affliction.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r2] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The name describes God as eternal, self-subsisting, one, and matchless in beauty and majesty; He is the ally of believers and kind even to sinful believers.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r3] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | When the Resurrection occurs, nothing can repel it.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r5] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | reports | The person on the path of soundness and uprightness reaches safety and honor; whoever deviates meets regret and loss, and the event distinguishes truth from pretense.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r6] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | reports | A poem says that when tears mingle on faces, one can distinguish a genuine mourner from someone pretending to weep.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:1-10/r1] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The Event is the coming of the Resurrection.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r1] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | The image of a docile dog and a thin calf alludes to a host's generosity and hospitality instead of stating those qualities directly.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r2] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | Ziyad's tent metonymically locates generosity, manliness, and giving in the praised person, just as the tent is pitched over him.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r3] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | Yazid ibn al-Hakam's poem about Ibn Yazid ibn al-Muhallab in al-Hajjaj's prison gives the captive virtues a setting parallel to the virtues placed in Ziyad's tent.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r4] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | The phrase about the dog being timid parallels a poem about restraining the dogs from barking: its docility is caused by the household's habitual restraint.

[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r6] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | Nasib says the patron's dog is more at ease with visitors than a mother with her daughter; the author links this to another poet's image of a dog almost greeting a guest.

[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r3] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | The Quran's inimitability cannot lie

[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p238#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · بعض المفسرين | reports | Some exegetes say it is the Rock of Jerusalem, which falls at the Resurrection; all these interpretations concern the Resurrection.
[TABRISI:56:1-16/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · أبو الحسن | reports | Abu al-Hasan analyzes the idhā in the cited Qur'anic phrase as genitive after hatta, so it is not adverbial. | mentions 10:22

[TABRISI:56:1-16/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | rejects | The author rejects as a grave error a contemporary grammarian's claim that Ibn Jinni made idhā rajjat govern idhā waqaʿat.

[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p612/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | The phrase waqaʿa kadhā can also mean that something happened; mawāqiʿ al-ghayth are places where rain falls.

[RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r10] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Al-Razi says Quran reading should be performed well and cites an Abu Dawud report from al-Baraʾ ibn ʿAzib, but its wording is cut off in this excerpt.

[RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r8] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A report from Ibn Umar says the Quran's companion is told to read, ascend and recite as he did in worldly life; no grading is stated.

[RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The previous sūra recounts blessings and demands gratitude rather than denial; this one describes good recompense for the grateful and bad recompense for those who deny.

[RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | One reading takes “the event” as the Resurrection or its earthquake: everyone will acknowledge it, denial will fail, unbelievers will be lowered in Hell, and believers raised in Paradise.
